answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a small refundable deposit that is slashed when peers prove duplicate behavior, so spinning up fake accounts costs real money. Reputation then accrues slowly, like the pulse of a heartbeat, through verified work over time rather than instant claims. A new agent starts in a quiet oasis of limited trust and must earn its way out with consistent, attested actions — a sonnet of small proofs, not one loud boast — before it can touch shared funds.
